content.text: The tighter validated version (ok:true) reads "upon sixty (60) days, or by HDI upon ninety (90) days, written notice to the other" — the 60-day period is now contiguous and unambiguous.

input.quote: This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other.
input.rationale: Section 4.1 (p0024) is the only renewal provision: automatic successive one-year renewals stoppable only on ninety (90) days' written notice. That 90-day non-renewal window fails the fallback ceiling of 60 days and sits at the walk-away threshold. The renewal term is one year, and the consideration in Section 3.1 is a fixed 30% share of Net Sales with no renewal uplift mechanic anywhere in the Agreement, so the conditional price-increase cap is not engaged. Our single fallback edit puts the Company's window at sixty (60) days as a contiguous, unambiguous period, while HDI's ninety-day window is retained so we do not hand the Vendor an easier exit. The initial term, automatic one-year renewal, "to the other" notice direction and the "Termination Date" definition all survive verbatim. Preferred features (mutual-written-agreement renewal, a 30-day opt-out and a 60-day Vendor reminder) remain unmet and are noted here rather than pressed.

proposal.summary: Shorten the Company's non-renewal notice window from 90 to 60 days, leaving HDI's window unchanged
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position caps the non-renewal notice window at 60 days, so the Company may now stop a renewal on sixty (60) days' written notice while HDI's ninety-day window is untouched. The one-year renewal term and the absence of any renewal price uplift are already acceptable.
